slides.title: Dispatch Copilot: launch, package and price

paragraphs.text: Dispatch Copilot: launch, package and price
Discussion document for the CEO and executive team, January 2027 planning
Brightwork
CEO and executive team
Synthetic benchmark data; every number from the briefing pack
Executive summary
Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, then restart the mobile rewrite
Copilot's value is real but demand is overstated: the $8M add-on case earns about $0.8M a year
–	Beta jobs per dispatcher-hour rose 11%, against 2% for matched accounts, among volunteers
–	Only 14% of beta accounts bought at $149; 46% of survey respondents said they would
AI must sit inside a plan; Pro at $12 more per seat beats the add-on if it wins twice the accounts
–	Recovering the win rate lost to Routewise is worth at most $0.6M of new ARR a year
–	Pro beats the add-on on ARR, gross profit and payback, but earns half as much per account
–	At the 2023 tier's 33% uptake, Pro adds about $2.9M of ARR, above the $2.3M the target needs
Pro needs a usage allowance, or heavy users would push company margin below the 75% floor
–	A top-decile account would cost 1.8 times in inference what an average account pays for Pro
–	An allowance of 333 requests per seat a month, with paid top-ups, keeps margin above 75%
Launch in Q2, then mobile in Q3: Copilot first wins while Pro uptake stays above 25%
–	Mobile reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as missing AI features
–	Making Pro wait two quarters costs 2.5 percentage points of NRR, against at most 1.9 for mobile
–	A Q1 test of both offers decides the package: Pro must win twice the add-on's accounts

It clears the $2.3M of expansion the 105% NRR target needs, which takes 26% uptake, on four assumptions
▪	33% of accounts move to Pro within a year, as they did to the 2023 higher tier, which had no AI; the Q1 offer test checks it
▪	Accounts that move have the average 6.2 seats (beta accounts averaged 8.1)
▪	Core keeps its $79 price, so no account pays more unless it chooses Pro
▪	No top-up revenue counted
1  NRR target: from 101% to 105% by 2028, i.e. 4 percentage points of today's $57.6M ARR. The live formula is in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook

▪	Top decile: these accounts sent 58% of all requests, so a flat price lets a few accounts absorb the margin

NRR forgone during a two-quarter delay, percentage points of NRR in the delay year, by sequence
Copilot first wins in the base case, but only narrowly
▪	Copilot first: the mobile cost is a ceiling; it assumes the rewrite would stop every mobile-driven churn on day one
▪	Mobile first at 33% uptake: gives up more NRR and leaves Routewise two more quarters as the only plan with AI inside
▪	Mobile first at 14% uptake: cheaper than Copilot first, which is why the Q1 offer test comes before the launch commitment
